declarations.name: Spec.predict_no_panic_spec
declarations.source_anchor: pub fn predict(a: usize, b: usize) -> Option<usize> {
declarations.lean_code:
/-- Property 3: `predict(a, b)` never panics, for every pair of `usize` values: no
out-of-bounds index, no division by zero and no arithmetic overflow can occur (nor any other
undefined behaviour); if the call returns, it returns normally. -/
def predict_no_panic_spec : Property := fun S =>
  -- For all `usize` values `a`, `b`,
  ∀ a b : Nat, a < 2 ^ 64 → b < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- given that the weight statics hold the tables of `src/weights.rs`,
    weightsStored S ⊢
      -- `predict(a, b)` does not panic: the only admitted outcome is a normal return.
      callPredict S a b (S.returns fun _ => ⌊True⌋)
declarations.description: For every pair of `usize` values `a`, `b`, `predict(a, b)` never panics: no out-of-bounds index, division by zero, arithmetic overflow, or other undefined behaviour occurs, and any return is a normal return. Premise: the `static` weight tables hold their compiled contents (`weightsStored`).

declarations.name: Spec.predict_out_of_range_spec
declarations.source_anchor: pub fn predict(a: usize, b: usize) -> Option<usize> {
declarations.lean_code:
/-- Property 2: if `a ≥ 113` or `b ≥ 113`, `predict(a, b)` returns `None` (and does not
panic). -/
def predict_out_of_range_spec : Property := fun S =>
  -- For all `usize` values `a`, `b`,
  ∀ a b : Nat, a < 2 ^ 64 → b < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- PRECONDITION: one of the inputs is at least the modulus `P = 113`;
    (113 ≤ a ∨ 113 ≤ b) →
    -- given that the weight statics hold the tables of `src/weights.rs`,
    weightsStored S ⊢
      -- `predict(a, b)` does not panic, and on return
      callPredict S a b (S.returns fun v =>
        -- POSTCONDITION: the result is `None`.
        ⌊v = noneUsize S⌋)
declarations.description: For every `usize` pair with `a >= 113` or `b >= 113`, `predict(a, b)` does not panic and, if it returns, returns `None`. Premise: the `static` weight tables hold their compiled contents (`weightsStored`).

declarations.name: Spec.predict_in_range_spec
declarations.source_anchor: pub fn predict(a: usize, b: usize) -> Option<usize> {
declarations.lean_code:
/-- Property 1: if `a < 113` and `b < 113`, `predict(a, b)` returns `Some((a + b) % 113)`
(and does not panic). -/
def predict_in_range_spec : Property := fun S =>
  -- For all `usize` values `a`, `b`,
  ∀ a b : Nat, a < 2 ^ 64 → b < 2 ^ 64 →
    -- PRECONDITION: both inputs are below the modulus `P = 113`;
    a < 113 → b < 113 →
    -- given that the weight statics hold the tables of `src/weights.rs`,
    weightsStored S ⊢
      -- `predict(a, b)` does not panic, and on return
      callPredict S a b (S.returns fun v =>
        -- POSTCONDITION: the result is `Some((a + b) % 113)`.
        ⌊v = someUsize S ((a + b) % 113)⌋)
declarations.description: For every `a < 113` and `b < 113`, `predict(a, b)` does not panic and, if it returns, returns `Some((a + b) % 113)`. Premise: the `static` weight tables of `src/weights.rs` hold their compiled contents (`weightsStored`).
